old_value: R 'Magic Damage' per sphere closes the burst
new_value: E applies cc_kind crowd control - setup before W

independent_computation.what_the_leaf_is: rotation.sources[] is the per-step rationale list of the derived cast order. The contract for these strings, quoted from the exported worklist that specifies the engine (data/worklists/f3-task.md, deliverable 1c and invariant 2b): 'EMIT a rationale string citing the specific atoms that drove the order' and 'the rationale cites real atoms'. A rationale is therefore correct only if (i) the atom/row it names exists in the cached data and (ii) the ordering claim it makes is supported by that data.

step_1_old_value_checked_against_wiki.claim: R deals 'Magic Damage' per sphere and closes the burst (R last).
step_1_old_value_checked_against_wiki.atom_exists: data/champions.json -> Syndra.abilities.R 'Unleashed Power' has a leveling row literally named 'Magic Damage per Sphere' = 80/120/160 (+20% AP). The quoted label is a real atomized row, not a paraphrase.
step_1_old_value_checked_against_wiki.per_sphere_semantics_verified: Wiki text: 'Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones. Afterwards, she barrages the target enemy champion with all collected Dark Spheres, each dealing magic damage upon hit.' 3 conjured + up to 4 grabbed = 3..7 spheres.

arithmetic_cross_check.conclusion: The per-sphere reading is arithmetically proven by the cached rows, and it proves R CONSUMES spheres already on the ground (min 3 = self-conjured only, max 7 = 4 pre-placed spheres from Q/W). An ability whose damage scales with what earlier casts left on the field must come last; 'closes the burst' is the data-correct placement. R also carries the 100-splinter execute ('execute the target if it would damage them to below 15% of their maximum health'), which is likewise a finisher, not an opener.

step_1_old_value_checked_against_wiki.verdict_on_old: Factually correct, cites a real atomized row, and states the ordering fact the data supports.

step_2_new_value_checked_against_wiki.claim_a: E applies crowd control  -> TRUE in substance. Wiki E 'Scatter the Weak': 'knocks them back for 400 units and up to 800 units away from Syndra' and 'Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds' (when a Dark Sphere is knocked into them).
step_2_new_value_checked_against_wiki.claim_b_the_defect: The CC type renders as the bare token 'cc_kind'. 'cc_kind' is not a crowd-control type; it is the name of a champion-module metadata FIELD. Quoted from data/worklists/f2-task.md: 'the champion modules in src/calculator/champions/ (options, parts with DamagePart metadata, dot_duration, post_hit_proc, empowers_next_auto, on_hit, cc_kind)', and data/champion-audit/batch-0.json: 'CC charm/slow (utility, cc_kind marker on E)'. The value of that field is a CC name. The canonical CC vocabulary in data/wiki-atoms/crowd-control-mobility.json is: Airborne, Blind, Cripple, Disarm, Disrupt, Drowsy, Sleep, Forced Action, Berserk, Charm, Flee, Taunt, Ground, Kinematics, Knockdown, Nearsight, Root, Silence, Polymorph, Slow, Stasis, Stun, Suspension, Suppression, ... Knockback. 'cc_kind' appears nowhere in it. Note the asymmetry with the old string, which quoted a real DATA VALUE ('Magic Damage'); the new string emits an unquoted FIELD NAME where the value belongs -- an unsubstituted template placeholder. The correct rendering for Syndra E would be 'stun' (1.25 s) or 'knockback'/'airborne', e.g. "E applies 'Stun' crowd control". As written the string cites no real atom and so fails the stated rationale invariant.
step_2_new_value_checked_against_wiki.claim_c_the_ordering: 'setup before W' is not supported by the cached data. A setup/consume edge requires the later ability to have a row/effect that consumes the applied state. Syndra W 'Force of Will' rows are 'Magic Damage' 70/100/130/160/190 (+65% AP), 'Bonus True Damage' (60-splinter Transcendent bonus, 12% + 2% per 100 AP) and 'Total Mixed Damage'; the wiki text for W ('telekinetically grabs the nearest Dark Sphere, enemy minion or non-epic monster ... Recast: throws the grabbed target ... All targets hit are slowed by 25% for 1.5 seconds') contains no enhanced/consume/vs-immobilized clause. Nothing in W consumes E's stun or knockback. The genuine setup/consume edges visible in the cached Syndra data run the other way: Q places Dark Spheres, which E needs in the cone to convert its knockback into the 1.25 s stun ('Dark Spheres can be knocked back ... Targets hit are also stunned for 1.25 seconds'), and which R grabs ('grabs up to 4 nearby live ones', proven by the 3x/7x arithmetic above). Additionally E's knockback (400-800 units) DISPLACES the target away from Syndra, which works against, not for, a subsequent W landing.
step_2_new_value_checked_against_wiki.verdict_on_new: Incorrect as written: placeholder instead of a real CC atom, plus an asserted E->W setup edge that the atomized data does not contain.

independent_computation.step_3_conclusion: At this leaf the old rationale is a verifiable, atom-cited, correctly-ordered statement (R's 'Magic Damage per Sphere' row; R consumes pre-placed spheres so it closes the burst). The new rationale replaces it with a string that names a metadata field rather than a crowd-control type and asserts an E-before-W setup relationship absent from the cached data. Old value stands.

notes: The literal token 'cc_kind' in the new value is the load-bearing defect: it is a field name, not a CC type, so the rationale cites no real atom. If the engine intended a substituted value, the wiki-correct rendering for Syndra E is 'Stun' (1.25 s) or 'Knockback'/'Airborne'.

Even with a correct CC name substituted, the ordering clause 'setup before W' would still lack data support: no Syndra W row or effect consumes a stun/knockback, while E's own stun is what DEPENDS on a Q-placed Dark Sphere.
